title: an Error class whose name is a non-ASCII TypeScript identifier is a nominal recoverable error like any other, and its lifted error variant carries its message
notes: Obligation: specification/failures.mdx, 'Error Classes': 'Any named class extending `Error` MUST be usable as a nominal recoverable error ... Authors MUST NOT need a `TaggedError("Name")` factory, `_tag` declaration, or separate error-declaration syntax. The compiler MUST provide stable nominal identity, matching metadata, serialization evidence, and cross-realm transport metadata while preserving ordinary `Error` behavior.' The obligation is over *any named class*, with no ASCII restriction stated. specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Source Relationship' adds that `.sm` differs from TypeScript only where explicitly documented, and TypeScript identifiers admit the full Unicode ID_Start/ID_Continue set; docs/DECISIONS.md 'Typed failures' (Locked) repeats the any-class rule. Written from the specification before it was run. The sibling case non-ascii-string-content-round-trips is the same program shape with an ASCII class name and non-ASCII *content*, and it passes on both backends — which isolates the identifier, not the source encoding, as the failing input. The `js` xfail here is RETIRED: the reference compiled this program clean and then threw `TypeError: invalid stable Error identity` from `registerErrorType` while the emitted module was still loading, because poc/src/runtime/errors.ts validated identities against an ASCII-only alphabet. The contract chosen is acceptance end to end, not a compile-time rejection — the class is legal TypeScript and the specification puts no ASCII restriction on it — so the validator's letter classes are now the Unicode ID_Start/ID_Continue ones. Widening is strictly additive: whitespace, quoting, control characters, structural punctuation, and over-length keys are still refused, and the identity still carries the class name verbatim rather than being encoded or hashed.
